mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 1% in the month prior to the prediction is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to reduced risk-free discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during periods of FEDFUNDS > 1%, or the S&P 500 20-day return is positive despite FEDFUNDS > 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment growth) of at least 50,000 jobs coinciding with a falling UNRATE (unemployment rate) signals labor market strengthening that boosts equity valuations, leading to positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly increase ≥ 50,000 AND UNRATE monthly decrease
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite the defined labor indicators moving in the predicted direction, or the interaction p-value exceeds 0.05 in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in GDPC1 (real private consumption) exceeding 2% for two consecutive months predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals robust consumer demand supporting equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during periods of strong GDPC1 growth, or the effect is not significant in a multiple regression controlling for FEDFUNDS and UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production index) below 97.5 suggests supply-side weakness that reduces corporate earnings expectations, producing a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during INDPRO < 97.5, or the effect is absent in periods of broader economic stability.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL (CPI) rises by more than 0.5% in a month, it indicates accelerating inflation, which is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investors discount future earnings more aggressively.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during CPIAUCSL > previous month + 0.5%, or the effect is not robust across multiple inflation spikes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in HOUST (housing starts) and increase in UNRATE (unemployment) indicates housing weakness and labor market stress, which together predict a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly decrease AND UNRATE monthly increase
regime_hint: Dual stress in housing and labor markets
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the defined interaction, or the interaction is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime where FEDFUNDS remains below 1% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to exhibit positive 20-day forward returns as lower discount rates boost equity present value.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the three-month low-rate window, or the effect is absent outside this regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RSAFS (retail sales) of over 10% for two consecutive months suggests weak consumer demand, which is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during periods of RSAFS decline, or the effect is not robust when controlling for broader macro variables.
